description: We are a sibling duo with big ambitions: one passionate programmer and one language student with a creative, global mindset. Together we bring creative solutions to worldwide change, and with Safe Horizon we turn NASA satellite data into a simple tool that keeps people safe.
summary:
Safe Horizon is an advanced wildfire monitoring platform that transforms NASA satellite observations into actionable environmental intelligence.

By combining 26 years of MODIS data with high-resolution VIIRS detections from NASA FIRMS, the platform identifies active wildfires, filters false alarms, and analyzes historical fire patterns. Advanced spatial clustering, nighttime fire activity analysis, and atmospheric modeling help assess fire intensity, potential risk zones, and smoke movement.

The project addresses the challenge by transforming complex Earth Observation datasets into accessible, near-real-time information that supports wildfire detection, disaster preparedness, climate research, and public safety.

Safe Horizon features an interactive 3D map, historical fire analysis, and a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides standardized access to processed satellite data for external applications and compatible systems.

Our goal is to bridge the gap between space-based observations and real-world decision-making, making wildfire intelligence more accessible, reliable, and actionable for everyone.
details:
WHAT DOES IT DO OR HOW DOES IT WORK?

Safe Horizon is an AI-powered wildfire monitoring platform that transforms NASA satellite data into actionable environmental intelligence.

It combines 26 years of MODIS observations with high-resolution VIIRS detections from NASA FIRMS. Using spatial clustering (DBSCAN), sensor validation, and thermal anomaly filtering, it identifies wildfire activity while reducing industrial false positives.

The platform also analyzes nighttime fire persistence (NWR), compares current activity against historical patterns using FireCal-H3, and estimates smoke movement using wind data and Sentinel-5P observations.

Results are delivered through an interactive 3D WebGL dashboard and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, allowing AI agents to access satellite intelligence directly.

WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

• Early detection of emerging wildfires using high-resolution VIIRS observations.

• Historical analysis based on 26 years of NASA satellite data.

• Reduced false alarms through intelligent filtering and multi-sensor validation.

• Smoke movement estimates and geospatial safety buffers.

• Direct integration with AI assistants through MCP.

WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT?

Safe Horizon aims to improve wildfire awareness, environmental research, and public safety.

It supports emergency responders with near-real-time fire information, helps researchers analyze long-term wildfire patterns, and enables communities and travelers to assess potential risks.

By connecting NASA Earth Observation data with AI systems, the project makes advanced satellite intelligence more accessible.

WHAT TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES DID YOU USE?

• Satellite Data: NASA FIRMS (MODIS, VIIRS), NASA GIBS, Copernicus Sentinel-5P and Sentinel-2.

• Weather Data: Meteomatics API.

• Development: TypeScript, Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, Shadcn UI.

• Geospatial: MapLibre GL JS, Turf.js, DBSCAN, Convex Hull, H3.

• AI Integration: Model Context Protocol (MCP), Streamable HTTP, Zod.

HOW IS YOUR PROJECT CREATIVE?

Safe Horizon combines three innovative approaches:

• AI-Native Satellite Intelligence: A native MCP server enables AI agents to independently query and analyze NASA Earth Observation data.

• FireCal-H3 & Nighttime Wildfire Ratio: Custom analytical methods compare current fire activity against historical patterns and identify persistent nighttime burning.

• Integrated Fire & Smoke Monitoring: Combines thermal detections, atmospheric observations, and wind conditions in one interactive platform.

WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM CONSIDER?

• Differences in MODIS and VIIRS spatial resolution.

• Eliminating industrial and non-wildfire thermal anomalies.

• Smoke hazards extending beyond active fire zones.

• Efficient processing of large satellite datasets.

• Scientific interpretability, scalability, and compatibility with open AI standards.
